title: the-loop-names-its-own-staleness-instead-of-benching-a-device
intention: When a probe cannot be loaded because THIS PROCESS is older than the code it is reading, the ground loop says that about ITSELF and does not bench the device — so the watch layer cannot be switched off by an ordinary rename.
why: BECAUSE IT ALREADY WAS, FOR 29 HOURS, AND NOTHING IN THE SYSTEM NOTICED. Fifteen devices carrying twenty-two probes — every WATCHME armed since 2026-08-13 15:35:43 — were skipped by the heartbeat for a defect that was never theirs. The lived symptom is not abstract: a build arms a watch, seals it, records it as PROVED, and the watch never fires once; the next mind reads a green record and a silent probe and has no way to tell that from a watch that fired and found nothing. Akien's standing frame, 2026-08-14: 'we keep on until this whole skills and mechanical workflow is solid' — and a watch layer a rename turns off is the least solid thing in it, because every WATCHME every future build arms lands in exactly the folder this defect darkens.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. A benched device emits nothing, so every watch behind it was an unmeasured claim wearing a sealed record's clothes.
Law 9 — red is the default and green is earned. Twenty-two probes read as green-and-quiet for 29 hours while never running; quiet was taken for earned.
Law 10 — nothing in the system is immeasurable. Every input to the missing predicate (process start time, file mtimes, the module file behind a class) was free on disk the whole time.
Akien 2026-08-14 — 'we keep on until this whole skills and mechanical workflow is solid'.
I-shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll — the staleness predicate runs only on the failure path, which is empty in the healthy case.

falsifier.proves_green: THREE PIECES AND THE THIRD IS WHAT MAKES THE FIRST TWO MORE THAN A NICER MESSAGE. (1) DETECT: on a probe-load failure, the loop evaluates one predicate — is this process older than the code it is judging — from the process start time, the mtime of the files involved, and, for the identity case, the module file behind the loaded class compared against the module file behind the loop's own. Both observed faces fall out of it: the isinstance mismatch where two module identities carry one class name, and the ImportError where a symbol exists on disk but not in the loaded module. (2) DO NOT BENCH: under that predicate the device is NOT held out and its probes still fire, because the device is not the failing party; a single trouble is raised against the LOOP instead, which is the one party it may make claims about (Law 6). (3) STILL FIRE: the tooth that keeps this honest is that a probe in the affected folder reaches its consumer after detection — a build that detects staleness, records it beautifully, and benches the device anyway leaves the outage exactly where it was.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) the staleness condition is constructed in a fixture and the device is benched anyway — the outage is unchanged and only the record got prettier; (2) the fix is a better error STRING, so a test that greps the message passes while twenty-two watches stay dark — the message was never the damage, the bench was; (3) the two observed faces are special-cased by symbol name or error text, so the next rename produces a third face and the loop blames the device again; (4) after detection, no probe from the affected folder reaches its consumer; (5) the loop raises the staleness trouble against a DEVICE rather than against itself; (6) the bench-from-live-tickets rule at loop.py:50 is weakened to make this easier — that rule is not the defect and is what made this outage reconstructable at all; (7) the ruled 5s liveness threshold is widened by this build for any reason.
falsifier.horizon: Now, and ahead of the constrain build that was next in Akien's order. The sequencing is not preference: constrain's WATCHME lands in a probes/ folder, and this ticket exists because that folder gets darkened by the loop's own staleness at the next code move. Building a watch into it first would arm a watch born dead — the same shape as the 22 already armed that way.

chart_notes.orient: The code is at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovery.py (load_module at :87, ProbeCache.probes_for at :114 where both the isinstance test at :146 and the import failure at :135 live) and cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/loop.py (_reconcile at :233, _bench and the TROUBLE_PREFIX rule at :49-52, _refresh_bench at :193). The trouble lane is cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py (raise_trouble :131, clear :194, live :233).
chart_notes.constrain: The 5s liveness threshold is RULED and is not in bounds. The bench-from-live-tickets rule is correct and must survive. ProbeCache's mtime keying is correct and must survive. The staleness predicate must run ONLY on the failure path so a green system pays nothing for it.
chart_notes.survey: Fifteen trouble records under CairnCommons/troubles/ground-loop-device-*.json now carry the full diagnosis in their cleared_by entries and are the primary evidence; commit c845ca4 in CairnCommons carries the timeline.
